canonical_definition:
What it is. Across papers, ARC-Easy is most commonly described as the easy split or easy subset of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, used as a multiple-choice science question answering benchmark. Definitions usually frame the items as grade-school or elementary-level science questions, often as easier than ARC-Challenge and sometimes as answerable with simple retrieval or text-matching, though some papers instead emphasize reasoning, commonsense reasoning, or basic factual knowledge. One paper gives the most specific dataset description, stating that the full ARC collection has 7,787 multiple-choice science exam questions and that the Easy subset contains 5,197 relatively easier questions; most reported uses are zero-shot, though one paper refers to ArcEasy-3-shots.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers use ARC-Easy to measure 13 constructs and 12 behavioral indicators, so the claimed target is spread across many framings rather than concentrated on a single one. The prevailing construct-level links are to Commonsense reasoning, Reasoning, and General ability, while the most frequent behavioral framings are multiple-choice question answering and question answering.

Space of uses. In use, papers usually position ARC-Easy as one element in broader zero-shot evaluation suites rather than as a standalone instrument. It is commonly paired with ARC-Challenge in reasoning and question-answering benchmark bundles. Papers also report ARC-Easy as measured by 3 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, and also OpenCompass and OLMES.

Concerns raised. A limited concern-related thread uses ARC-Easy in studies of data contamination and benchmark overfitting, where papers evaluate contamination effects on benchmark mixes that include ARC-Easy. Papers otherwise do not explicitly describe additional instrument-specific concerns.

characterization_sections.label: What it is.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, ARC-Easy is most commonly described as the easy split or easy subset of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, used as a multiple-choice science question answering benchmark. Definitions usually frame the items as grade-school or elementary-level science questions, often as easier than ARC-Challenge and sometimes as answerable with simple retrieval or text-matching, though some papers instead emphasize reasoning, commonsense reasoning, or basic factual knowledge. One paper gives the most specific dataset description, stating that the full ARC collection has 7,787 multiple-choice science exam questions and that the Easy subset contains 5,197 relatively easier questions; most reported uses are zero-shot, though one paper refers to ArcEasy-3-shots.

characterization_sections.label: What it is claimed to measure.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use ARC-Easy to measure 13 constructs and 12 behavioral indicators, so the claimed target is spread across many framings rather than concentrated on a single one. The prevailing construct-level links are to Commonsense reasoning, Reasoning, and General ability, while the most frequent behavioral framings are multiple-choice question answering and question answering.

characterization_sections.label: Space of uses.
characterization_sections.text: In use, papers usually position ARC-Easy as one element in broader zero-shot evaluation suites rather than as a standalone instrument. It is commonly paired with ARC-Challenge in reasoning and question-answering benchmark bundles. Papers also report ARC-Easy as measured by 3 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, and also OpenCompass and OLMES.

characterization_sections.label: Concerns raised.
characterization_sections.text: A limited concern-related thread uses ARC-Easy in studies of data contamination and benchmark overfitting, where papers evaluate contamination effects on benchmark mixes that include ARC-Easy. Papers otherwise do not explicitly describe additional instrument-specific concerns.
